prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat electronic bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle graphene, opening moiré quantum matter

statement.case_for: I keep B014 as my single-part preferred prize. The scientific case is a quantitative electronic-structure prediction, the 2011 Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model with flat bands at a specific twist angle, that was tested by an experiment which could have failed: the 2018 observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle devices by Jarillo-Herrero's group. Many independent groups reproduced the central phenomena within a few years and extended them to other moiré systems and to fractional and topological states, so the discovery stands whatever the pairing mechanism turns out to be. A prize here would reward a new tunable platform and not an explanation, and the citation I propose is deliberately worded around the flat-band prediction and the observed correlated states, as Mehlig and Lindroth asked, so that the unsettled mechanism does not enter the claim. Round 1 did not change my ranking, but it changed how I weigh the opposing case. Johansson, Kroll and Lindroth are right that the pending redefinition of the second is an application and not a condition for the validity of the lattice clock, and I withdraw the part of my opening reservation that treated it as a maturity problem. B005 is a mature, tightly credited and genuinely distinct invention, and I regard it as the committee's strongest alternative. My remaining difference with its supporters is the criterion, not the facts: I give more weight to a recent discovery that changed what condensed-matter physicists work on and that is moving fast now, and I see no reason why waiting would make the credit for B014 cleaner.
statement.case_against: The strongest points against my position are the ones colleagues pressed. The experiments are about eight years old, the origin of the superconductivity and the nature of several correlated phases are unresolved, and sample variability, strain and disorder still matter, so a committee that wants a settled interpretation can fairly say it is early. The credit is also an incomplete allocation: Yuan Cao, lead author of the 2018 papers, other experimental groups such as Cory Dean's, and the earlier twisted-bilayer band-structure theorists (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) are outside the three names, and I cannot settle the priority question from the supplied material; my view that the 2011 model gave the first quantitative magic-angle flat-band condition is from recollection. By comparison B005 needs only two names and has two decades of independent confirmation. If the committee concludes that a clean credit and a long track record must outrank novelty of phenomenon, B005 is the defensible choice and I would not obstruct it.

responses.point: Kroll argues that the pairing mechanism in twisted bilayer graphene is still unsettled and Cao is outside the trio, so the maturity case for B014 is weaker than for B005, and that the SI redefinition should not govern the timing of a Nobel decision.
responses.response: I accept the second half completely: the clock was established by independent laboratories reaching and surpassing 1e-18, and the redefinition is an institutional process, so my opening ranking of B005 sixth was too low and I now treat it as the closest competitor to my own choice. On the first half I still disagree about what is being rewarded. The observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity at the magic angle is stable and widely reproduced irrespective of the mechanism, just as the discovery of high-temperature superconductivity was recognised before it was explained. I would concede that the credit is the harder part of B014 than of B005, and I do not claim otherwise.

responses.point: Olsson ranks B014 second and would support it only if the committee states openly in the citation that the superconducting mechanism is unresolved, citing sample variability, strain and disorder as reasons for caution on maturity.
responses.response: I think your condition is reasonable and my citation already meets it: it claims the prediction of flat bands and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, and says nothing about pairing. I would accept making that restraint explicit in the committee's public explanatory text. Sample dependence is real, but it is also the reason the moiré platform keeps producing new phases, and the central features of the 2018 phase diagram have been seen by several independent groups. We agree on the facts; the open question is how much weight an unresolved mechanism should carry, and I would give it less than you do.

responses.point: Mehlig frames the choice as a new-phenomenon prize against a measurement-science prize, and notes that Lopes dos Santos and colleagues had a flat-band-type result before 2011 so the earlier theory credit should not be discounted lightly.
responses.response: I agree that the choice is that one, and I also accept the correction on earlier theory: it should be stated as a cost of B014 and not waved away. My defence is the narrow one that you also gave: the 2011 continuum model supplied the quantitative magic-angle condition that the experiment then tested, which is why the citation is worded around flat bands at the magic angle and not around twisted bilayers in general. I continue to disagree with your earlier two-name idea, since Bistritzer is first author on the continuum-model calculation and dropping him buys nothing inside a three-seat limit, and I am glad you have now accepted all three names.

responses.point: Johansson says the experimental credit for B014 leaves out Cao and Dean, would credit the pair or the trio only if the 2011 model is judged a joint result, and finds the clock credit cleaner.
responses.response: The 2011 paper is a joint result, with Bistritzer and MacDonald as the authors of the continuum model, so by your own condition the trio holds. I maintain that Dean's hBN moiré work is a separate and related line that should not displace the magic-angle discovery, and that a Nobel Prize normally credits the group leader. I do concede that omitting Cao is an arguable cut, and that on credit alone B005 is cleaner; our disagreement is whether that advantage should decide the matter.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct conceptual step from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes and that waiting for the SI redefinition would tie the prize to a metrological schedule.
responses.response: I agree with both points and they weakened my reservations about B005. The distinction between the comb, single-ion control and many-atom lattice interrogation is a real one and the overlap worry is smaller than I felt on opening. I would still note that if B005 is chosen, the committee should keep the citation narrow and decide in advance how it treats Ye's share as co-invention or record-accuracy realization, a question Danielsson also raised.

uncertainties: Whether Yuan Cao or another experimental group has a claim strong enough to change the experimental seat; this cannot be settled from the supplied credited names.

Whether the earlier twisted-bilayer band-structure theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) changes the theory credit; my reading that the 2011 continuum model is decisive is from recollection and is unverified.
Whether the unresolved superconducting mechanism will change how decisive the 2018 discovery looks later, and whether eight years is enough maturity for this committee.

Whether the committee prefers a settled measurement-science invention (B005) or a younger new-phenomenon discovery (B014); this is a question of criterion on which I may be weighting the field I know best.
statement.conflict_note: No documented personal or institutional tie to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer is apparent from my profile. I work on electronic-structure theory of two-dimensional materials at Uppsala and chaired the committee in the 2025 cycle; the field proximity to B014 is not a recusal ground but I flag it so that colleagues can test my judgment against B005, which is outside my field. I have no documented tie to Katori or Ye either. No change from round 1.
